clue.text: Run towards this place almost more willingly

parts.note: R is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a run
at, as in throwing something at a target, means towards it

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word for this place is left off

parts.note: this place is here

explanation.surface: Someone is told to hurry over here, and nearly with more enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: Rather as in 'I would rather go' expresses preference, so it means more gladly or willingly.

clue.text: Really dislike expression of sympathy put on by British men

indicators.note: when the British letter puts the sigh on like a garment, the sigh wraps around it

parts.note: ah is a sigh of sympathy
OR, other ranks, is the military term for ordinary soldiers, i.e. men

explanation.surface: Someone loathes the sympathetic noises British men make as a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put on' reads as 'pretended', but here it is wearing: British (B) wears AH, so AH goes around B.
explanation.definitionFit: To abhor something is to loathe it, a strong synonym for really disliking it.

clue.text: What marks out grave aspect of leader?

parts.note: a leader is a head; 'of leader' makes it possessive, head's
tone means character or aspect, as in the tone of a meeting

explanation.surface: A question about a solemn quality in a leader's manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grave aspect' looks like a serious look; 'grave' belongs to the definition, the burial place, and 'aspect of leader' is HEAD'S TONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A headstone is the stone slab placed at the head of a grave to mark where someone is buried.

clue.text: Spots case for employer being less prudent

parts.note: a rash is an outbreak of spots on the skin

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer shell, so its first and last letters are taken

explanation.surface: An employee with spots puts their case to the boss for some reason.
explanation.definitionFit: Rasher is the comparative of rash, meaning more reckless and hasty, the opposite of prudent.

clue.text: Relative acquires fashionable cycling strip

indicators.note: acquires means the relative takes the other letters into itself

parts.note: an uncle is a relative

indicators.note: cycling means the letters go round, the first moving to the end

parts.note: hot means fashionable, in demand

explanation.surface: A relative buys a trendy cycling kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cycling strip' looks like a bike jersey; 'strip' is the definition and 'cycling' turns HOT into OTH.
explanation.definitionFit: To unclothe someone is to remove their clothes, which is to undress or strip them.

clue.text: University attendance hit badly over university not having legal status

indicators.note: over means the jumbled letters lie across and around the second university letter
badly means the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: U again stands for university

explanation.surface: A university's attendance figures suffer, leaving it without legal recognition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit badly' rearranges ATTENDANCE HIT into NATHENTICATED, which goes around the second U after the opening U.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unauthenticated has not been officially verified, so it lacks validity or legal standing.

clue.text: Closed firm's chance deal, without terms of extra quota changing

indicators.note: changing means the letters of the phrase are reshuffled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: the terms of a word here are its endings, the last letter of each

parts.note: its last letter A
its last letter A

explanation.surface: A company made a lucky deal, though the extra quota terms didn't change.
explanation.walkthrough: Shuffle CHANCE DEAL with the two A's that end extra and quota taken out; 'firm' supports the definition, a fist closed firmly.
explanation.definitionFit: Clenched fists or teeth are tightly closed, shut hard together.

clue.text: Golden rule primarily circumscribed by line competitors must not cross

indicators.note: circumscribed by means surrounded by, so the line goes around the letter

parts.note: the oche is the line darts players stand behind when throwing

indicators.note: primarily means just the first letter

explanation.surface: A golden rule, first of all: competitors must never step over the line.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCHE is the throwing line in darts, a pub game much played in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is a yellow-brown earth pigment, so as a colour it is a golden yellow shade.

clue.text: Previously let deer breed round November

parts.note: a hind is a female deer

indicators.note: round means the breed word goes around the November letter

parts.note: a race is a breed or stock
N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Deer were formerly allowed to breed in late autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let' looks like 'allowed'; it is the old noun for an obstacle, still heard in 'without let or hindrance'.
explanation.definitionFit: In older English a let was an impediment or obstruction, which is what a hindrance is.

clue.text: Who possibly saved regularly and kept cash?

definitions.text: Who possibly saved regularly and kept cash?

indicators.note: possibly means the letters could be arranged another way
regularly means every other letter is taken

parts.note: its second and fourth letters A and E
taken as written for the shuffle

explanation.surface: A question about the sort of person who saves steadily and hoards money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges AE (alternate letters of saved) with KEPT CASH, and the whole clue describes the miser.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheapskate is a stingy person, exactly someone who scrimps and hoards money rather than spend it.

clue.text: Imply gangland killing involves money essentially

indicators.note: involves means the killing word takes the other letter inside it

parts.note: a hit is a contract killing by gangsters

indicators.note: essentially means the central letter, the essence of the word

explanation.surface: Suggest that a gang murder has money at its heart.
explanation.definitionFit: To hint is to suggest something indirectly, which is to imply it.

clue.text: Fuss over that woman's most disrespectful

indicators.note: over means the fuss word goes over and around the other piece

parts.note: to fret is to fuss or worry
that woman's is she's

explanation.surface: Fussing about how rude that woman is.
explanation.definitionFit: Fresh can mean cheeky or impudent, so freshest is the most impertinent or disrespectful.

clue.text: 22 holding attention briefly and bringing happiness

indicators.note: holding means the cry word wraps around the next piece

parts.note: 22 refers to SHOUT, whose synonym here is cry

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: heed is attention, as in 'pay heed'

explanation.surface: A shout that grabs attention for a moment and lifts spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cheery is bright and cheerful, so it spreads good humour and joy.

clue.text: Part of apocryphal observation?

indicators.note: part of means the answer is a run of letters inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word into the second

explanation.surface: A query about a fragment of some doubtful remark.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters straddle the two words; the clue also hints at the halo seen in saintly pictures, an unverified, apocryphal vision.
explanation.definitionFit: A halo is a ring of light shown around a holy head, often in stories of uncertain truth.

clue.text: Volcano with molten rock rising, ejecting tons round constant hot flood

indicators.note: round means the reversed letters go around the next pair
ejecting means throwing out the letter that stands for tons
rising, in a down clue, means the letters read upwards, backwards

parts.note: Etna is the volcano in Sicily
lava is molten rock
C is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A volcano erupts, molten rock pouring forth in a hot flood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' turns ETNA LAVA into AVALANTE; 'ejecting tons' drops the T, giving AVALANE, which goes round CH.
explanation.definitionFit: An avalanche is a sudden overwhelming mass of something, so figuratively a deluge or flood.

clue.text: Jumbo jet plane crashed leaving Jack outside hospital

indicators.note: outside means the reworked letters surround the hospital letter
crashed means the letters are smashed into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
J is the card abbreviation for jack
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A jumbo jet crashes, missing someone called Jack, who is outside the hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumbo jet' looks like one phrase; 'Jumbo' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumbo was a famous zoo elephant, and the name became a general nickname for any elephant.

clue.text: Husband richer after leaving wife in a better position financially

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for husband in records

indicators.note: after leaving means the wife letter has gone from the richer word

parts.note: wealthier means richer

explanation.surface: A husband becomes richer after his wife walks out, leaving him better off.
explanation.definitionFit: A healthier balance sheet or bank account is a stronger one, so it means better off in money terms.

clue.text: Set free naked hunter gatherer taking sides once more

indicators.note: naked means stripped of its outer layer, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: the word whose inside is kept

indicators.note: taking sides means losing the outer letters, and once more means doing so a second time

parts.note: lose its outer letters twice

explanation.surface: A naked hunter-gatherer picks sides again, like early humans.
explanation.walkthrough: Stripping GATHERER gives ATHERE; stripping again gives THER.
explanation.definitionFit: To untether an animal is to undo the rope holding it, releasing it.

clue.text: Production of large plant left behind film fan

indicators.note: behind means the left letter comes after the film word

parts.note: a haze is a thin film or mist
a nut is an enthusiast or fan, as in a fitness nut

explanation.surface: Making a large plant: the film fan got left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film fan' looks like a movie buff; the film is a haze and the fan is a nut.
explanation.definitionFit: The hazel is a large shrub or small tree, and this nut is what it produces.

clue.text: What stops old lady going the other way?

definitions.text: What stops old lady going the other way?

indicators.note: going the other way means the whole result is read backwards
stops means the what word plugs a gap in the old lady word

parts.note: ma, mother, is slang for one's old lady
eh? is said to mean what?

explanation.surface: A question about what might halt an old woman walking the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the polite cough you would give to stop her.
explanation.definitionFit: Ahem is the throat-clearing cough used to attract attention or halt someone politely.

clue.text: Distinguishing mark of each criminal imprisoned by court

indicators.note: imprisoned by means locked inside the court letters
criminal means the letters are bent out of shape

explanation.surface: Every criminal locked up by the court bears a distinguishing mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A cachet is a seal or stamp, and by extension a mark of distinction or prestige.

clue.text: Lashes out in struggle

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of their usual order

explanation.surface: Someone strikes out wildly during a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A hassle is a bother or difficult effort, so a struggle.

clue.text: Mum, I want you to go and buy drinks for everyone

parts.note: mum means silent, as in 'mum's the word', and sh is a call for silence
'Out!' is the curt order that sends someone away

explanation.surface: Telling Mum to leave so you can stand everyone a round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' looks like a mother; it means keep quiet. To shout is British and Australian slang for buying a round of drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: In pub slang, your shout is your turn to pay for the round, treating the whole group.

clue.text: Island surrounded by continent? Correct

indicators.note: surrounded by means the island letters are enclosed by the continent word

parts.note: continent here is the adjective meaning self-restrained, sexually abstinent, i.e. chaste
IS is the map abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: Is an island ringed by a continent? Correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Continent' wants to be a landmass beside 'Island'; it is the adjective for self-restrained.
explanation.definitionFit: To correct a wrongdoer in the old sense is to punish or rebuke them, which is to chastise.

clue.text: Polish hotel's dated exterior

indicators.note: exterior means the dated word is on the outside, round the hotel letter

parts.note: if two people have been seeing each other they have dated, so seen
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet; 's is has

explanation.surface: A Polish hotel has an old-fashioned facade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' as a nationality is the false path; it is the shine on a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheen is lustre or gloss, the shine that polishing produces.

clue.text: Repeat section of repetitive chorus

indicators.note: section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Sing again part of a song's repeated refrain.
explanation.definitionFit: To echo is to reproduce a sound or words again, which is to repeat them.

clue.text: Travels freely in India having been beset by delays around Hong Kong

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded, so the India letter ends up inside the rest
around means the delays word goes round the Hong Kong letters

parts.note: hitches are snags or delays
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Backpacking around India with plenty of delays near Hong Kong.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who hitchhikes travels by getting free lifts from passing drivers.

clue.text: Harassed Conservative rushed to stop introduction of higher education

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its first letter
to stop means to plug the gap, sitting inside the other letters

parts.note: tore means rushed, as in 'tore down the road'

explanation.surface: A Tory hurried to block the start of university education and was harassed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Higher education' reads as one phrase, but only the H of higher is taken, with ED for education.
explanation.definitionFit: To hector is to bully or badger with blustering talk, so hectored means harassed.

clue.text: Dictator's projected king's power

indicators.note: a dictator dictates, speaking aloud, so this signals a sound-alike

parts.note: projected means hurled, i.e. thrown

explanation.surface: A tyrant's planned grab for royal power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dictator' looks like a tyrant; it is someone dictating, speaking words aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: The throne stands by metonymy for sovereign authority, the power of the monarch.
